治疗装置作为促进食管语音获得的辅助资源

Therapeutic device as a facilitating resource for esophageal voice acquisition.

中文摘要

目的：描述使用一种用于直接食管刺激的治疗装置的发现，该装置可促进食管语音的产生。方法：15名全喉切除受试者参与研究，这些受试者均无语音产生，且传统言语-语言病理学疗法在食管语音获得方面未获成功。受试者在接受该装置进行12次食管刺激之前和之后，接受了针对全喉切除的特定嗓音质量方案、视频荧光镜检查以及嗓音自我评估问卷的评估。为刺激食管语音获得，使用一根总长度为50 cm的导管进行直接食管刺激，该导管从鼻孔引入直至到达咽食管段；导管的另一端固定于气管造口。干预连续进行12周，无中断。采用描述性和推断性统计分析，显著性水平为5%。结果：9名（60%）受试者发展出可用于交流的有效食管语音，而6名（40%）受试者成功发展出食管声音。听觉-感知评估未显示干预前后时刻之间存在统计学显著差异；然而，参与者的自我评估表明其感知到嗓音质量有所改善。结论：使用所提出装置进行食管刺激与患者自我评估的改善相关，并使一部分受试者能够实现功能性食管语音。该装置可能代表一种可行的治疗资源。

英文摘要

To describe the findings on the use of a therapeutic device for direct esophageal stimulation, which facilitates the production of the esophageal voice. Fifteen total laryngectomized subjects, with no voice production and no success in traditional speech-language pathology therapies for esophageal voice acquisition, participated. Subjects were evaluated using a specific vocal quality protocol for total laryngectomy, videofluoroscopy, and a vocal self-assessment questionnaire before and after 12 sessions of esophageal stimulation with the device. To stimulate esophageal voice acquisition, direct esophageal stimulation was performed using a catheter with a total length of 50 cm, which was introduced from the nostril until reaching the pharyngoesophageal segment; the other end of the catheter was fixed to the tracheostoma. The intervention occurred over 12 consecutive weeks, without interruption. Descriptive and inferential statistical analysis was performed at a 5% significance level. Nine (60%) subjects developed effective esophageal voice for communication, while 6 (40%) managed to develop esophageal sound. Auditory-perceptual evaluation did not show statistically significant differences between pre- and post-intervention moments; however, participants' self-assessment indicated perceived improvement in vocal quality. Esophageal stimulation with the proposed device was associated with improvements in patients' self-assessment and enabled a proportion of subjects to achieve functional esophageal voice. The device may represent a feasible therapeutic resource. 2B - Prospective interventional study without control group.
